name: Iris
tagline: Self-hosted phone remote for coding agents with cost-aware routing
pitch: Iris is a self-hosted phone remote (PWA) for coding agents with cost-aware routing: proteus picks the cheapest sufficient leg, chrysaor optionally fronts a litellm pool on localhost, ACP unlocks many CLIs, and e2ee pairing keeps the host off the public internet — no Iris account, no hosted backend.
features: Cost-aware routing (proteus) — cheapest agent that can finish the prompt
Transparent dollars and tokens on the remote before you send
Direct or pool topology; chrysaor + litellm bound to 127.0.0.1 only
ACP multi-agent unlock plus native legs where needed
E2EE pairing, transport ladder, ledger calibration, handoff on quota exhaustion
quick_start: Clone the repo and run `pnpm install`.
Read `docs/STATE.md`, then `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md` for the next sprint.
Run `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test`. Pages demo: https://edwardlthompson.github.io/iris/
install: Node 22+ and pnpm. `pnpm install` at the repo root. Optional LiteLLM for pool topology binds to 127.0.0.1 only — see docs/BUILD_PLAN.md.
usage: Start the host daemon, pair the phone PWA over LAN, send prompts with the cost chip visible. Choose direct or pool per repo. Agents: one sprint per session from docs/BUILD_PLAN.md.
